A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete 28-page document, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered page bodies match throughout; differences are confined to publication-status and arXiv version/date markings.

before.justification: v1 reports original RNN simulations and analyses of swap errors and neural representations in Section 4, plus multisensory cue-combination experiments in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original simulation and analysis results in Section 4 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The dendritic RNN architecture, synthetic behavioural data generation, diffusion-based objective, teacher forcing, and task-specific adaptations are identical in both versions.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same index-cued and feature-cued visual working-memory tasks, macaque-data comparisons, and multisensory cue-combination task in Appendix F.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including task-optimal networks and diffusion-trained networks with no swaps, constant swap probability, or a smooth swap function in Figure 8 and Table 1.

E3.justification: Task durations, training budgets, model sizes, evaluation procedures, and metrics are unchanged. This includes the cue-space KS evaluation in Appendix F and the settings in Table 2.

E4.justification: Both versions retain identical noise and probe-distance ablations, optimisation-window comparisons, and representational-geometry analyses in Figure 3 and Appendices C–E.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including Figure 4's mean and standard deviation across spatial configurations. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical and graphical results match, including swap-rate fits, neural-geometry comparisons, Table 1 values, and the posterior-distribution and KS results in Figures 13–14.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, and derivations are identical, including the BNS formulation, network dynamics, training objectives, and Bayesian cue-combination model.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain identical claims about synthetic behavioural training data, diffusion-based RNN training, and discovering neural mechanisms of cognitive errors.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the proposed swap-error mechanisms, dependence on a generative behavioural model, and need for experimental verification and further dynamical analysis.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information in Appendices B, D, F, and G is identical, including hardware, optimiser, batch sizes, training times, hyperparameters, and noise schedules.

R1.justification: The cited works and comparisons with prior approaches are identical. The updated publication-status header does not revise the paper's scientific positioning.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint. Under review.' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'. The arXiv stamp changes from v1, 4 Dec 2025 to v2, 22 Feb 2026. Body wording and document organisation are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–15, Tables 1–2, captions, equations, and their placement are identical. The header and version-stamp wording updates do not alter the page structure or figure/table presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 updates publication-status and version/date markings only. The scientific text, results, appendices, and visual presentation remain identical, establishing no meaningful difference in clarity, evidential support, or reproducibility.
